title: Variant interchangeability validation and tooling parity maintenance
creator: Lucas Nguyen
description: Maintain and validate a compatibility matrix that guarantees safe interchangeability between primary models and fallback variants used by Smart Routing policies. Scope covers tokenizer parity, context/KV cache alignment, tool-calling surface consistency, and CI tooling to detect regressions. The matrix powers automated fallback decisions for region selection and tier routing: mismatches currently lead to truncation, tokenization drift, or tool-call schema errors when requests failover. This ticket formalizes validation checks, remediation steps, and a rollout path for automated checks in the runtime CI and the console validation UI.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical compatibility matrix exists as a machine-readable artifact in the repo (CSV/JSON) mapping primary models to approved fallback variants and the specific compatibility flags (tokenizer, context-window, KV-schema, tool-IO).

Automated CI job added to runtime-tests that runs tokenizer equivalence tests and KV replay scenarios for each primary/fallback pair; CI fails if tokenization drift > 0.5% or KV schema mismatch is detected.
A lightweight in-console validator surfaces potential incompatibilities for a configured allotment (region/tier/model-set) with links to remediation PRs or recommended variant choices.
A remediation playbook (doc) with test artifacts and a sample PR template is available and linked from the matrix for each incompatibility type.
No customer-facing fallback incidents attributable to tokenizer or KV mismatches in the 30 days after rollout for routes covered by canary policy.

updates: 2026-02-06: Kickoff meeting notes - aligned on scope to include tokenizer hash and KV schema versioning. Decided not to block routing when only minor tokenizer drift is present; instead add scoring and warning. Action: Sara to produce initial inventory.

2026-02-14: Inventory complete. Found 18 primary->fallback pairs with missing KV schema metadata. Raised quick fixes for 6 variants that lack tool-call signature declarations. See GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/4589

2026-02-20: Tokenizer equivalence runner prototype merged to feature/tokenizer-checker (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4620). Early runs show a single open-source variant with 1.7% tokenization drift for long inputs; flagged for deeper review.

2026-02-24: KV-replay harness initial tests executed against 200 sample traces from production-like generator. Two variants exhibit KV eviction behavior at shorter contexts. Decided remediation options: increase max_context_tokens for fallback or avoid that fallback for long-sequence routes.

2026-03-01: CI job added as experimental non-blocking job on main (runtime-tests/tokenizer-check); next step: make it blocking for flagged high-risk routes after two weekly green runs. Assigned follow-up task to CI Platform.
